title: Establish runtime compatibility declarations and onboarding checklist for third-party weights
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Community and third-party model weights are entering the catalog with inconsistent metadata about runtime assumptions (sequence length, kv-cache compatibility, required ops/kernels, quantization formats). This causes runtime misconfigurations, failed deployments, and surprise regressions for customers. Goal: define a minimal, machine-parseable "compatibility declaration" schema and a lightweight onboarding checklist so PMs/ENG/design can consistently validate new entries before publication. Deliverables: 1) PRD describing declaration fields and pass/fail rules; 2) onboarding checklist for intake reviewers; 3) UI changes to surface compatibility fields in catalog; 4) gating rule for hosted ingestion pipeline that alerts and optionally blocks unfilled required fields. Stakeholders: Catalog PM (Maya), Runtime leads (Jonas Becker), Onboarding eng (Rafael Gomez), Security/compliance (Sana Iqbal), Developer docs (Aaron Lee). Success metric: reduce runtime incompatibility incidents from community models by 80% within 3 months of rollout.
scope: Define compatibility declaration schema (required + optional fields)
Create a 7-step onboarding checklist used by intake reviewers
Add two new required fields in model catalog UI: 'compatibility_level' and 'pinned_runtime_constraints'
Introduce a pre-ingest validation hook in the hosted pipeline that emits warnings and blocks when required fields are missing
Publish a short guidance doc and intake template for community contributors
out_of_scope: Automatic runtime-side enforcement for Private deployments on day one
Automatic conversion/quantization of weights during onboarding
Full static graph analysis for operator-level compatibility (deferred to research)
acceptance_criteria: A machine-parseable 'compatibility_declaration' schema (JSON Schema text) exists in the catalog spec and is checked by ingest pipeline
The catalog UI shows 'compatibility_level' (enum: 'verified', 'best-effort', 'experimental') and 'pinned_runtime_constraints' (free text + structured list) on the model entry page
Onboarding checklist (7 items) is used for the next 10 intake tickets and documented as the canonical process
Ingest pipeline emits a blocking error for new hosted entries missing required 'compatibility_declaration' fields; non-blocking warnings for optional fields
A short Confluence guidance page and template are published and linked from the catalog entry flow
At least one runtime team sign-off (ENG) and one security reviewer sign-off recorded before non-experimental models are published
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Blocking ingest on required fields could slow community contributions. Mitigation: staged rollout — first surface warnings for 2 weeks, then enforce blocking for new entries after we have docs and examples.

Risk: Runtime team may not have bandwidth to validate operator-level claims. Mitigation: require only high-level runtime signals (kv-cache support, seq-len tested to N, quant formats supported), escalate complex claims to research with a 'experimental' tag.
Risk: UX friction for catalog contributors. Mitigation: provide pre-filled templates and examples, and a small 'fast-track' review queue for partners.
Risk: Security implications of third-party weights (licensing, trojan risk). Mitigation: require a security checklist step and sign-off when a model is marked 'verified'
notes_and_decisions: Decision: compatibility_declaration will be JSON Schema v7 to keep validation tooling simple and existing library support
Decision: initial required fields will be minimal: 'tested_seq_length', 'kv_cache_compatible', 'supported_quant_formats', 'notes_on_constraints'
Trade-off: We will not attempt operator-level bytecode validation in this phase to ship quickly and reduce blocker surface
Agreed: 'pinned_runtime_constraints' is both a structured list and free-text field so we can capture edge cases in reviewer notes
